gainRange.assumption: If a settled exit recovers to +1 m/s over a modestly shorter distance, capped by sustained same-speed acceleration already recorded on the fastest lap; available traction remains unverified.
gainRange.method: Measured recovery window 10.6 m; a desired recovery shape compressed by up to15% is capped by the recorded acceleration and lateral-demand envelopes before computing any saving. Conditional fixed-distance integral of 1/v over the measured minimum-to-+1 m/s window. Compress the recorded speed-versus-distance shape by at most 15%, using the recorded same-speed acceleration envelope as a cap, then hold its recorded final speed to the original endpoint. Minimum speed, final speed and all speeds outside the window are preserved; no profile extrapolation. No faster lap validates this scenario, and the recovery duration is not time saved. Scenario choices are not confidence bounds or an achievable forecast; coarse GPS curvature must ease or remain stable; candidate lateral demand cannot exceed the recorded window maximum and longitudinal acceleration cannot exceed sustained same-speed measured capacity. Grip and control causes remain unverified; this is not a safe-speed instruction. Aggregation uses only disjoint endpoint-preserving scenarios.
